races.paceDynamic: Purple Owl is marked as a non-runner, removing the only confirmed front runner from this field. Washington Singer and Jamaicaine will likely take up the early running from their prominent styles, but neither is a natural pace-forcer which creates a moderate tempo. With most runners (Hillsin, Bread And Butter, Herbygoesbananas, Marhaba Million, Mistress Fox) adopting hold-up tactics, the race will develop into a patient affair with the bulk of the field tracking the leaders through steady fractions. This tactical setup strongly favours prominent runners who can position handy and kick, as they'll avoid the inevitable traffic problems that will engulf the large pack of hold-up horses in the home straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Washington Singer and Jamaicaine control the pace from the front without pressure
scenarios.body: The moderate gallop allows both to conserve energy while the hold-up brigade gets shuffled back, creating a two-horse battle where tactical positioning trumps finishing kick. Washington Singer's recent Plumpton form and Jamaicaine's hat-trick ability make them perfectly suited to exploit this scenario.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes genuinely slow and compacts the field
scenarios.body: The patient tempo allows the back-markers to close up and unleash their finishing kicks simultaneously, creating a cavalry charge finish where the best stayer prevails. Mistress Fox benefits from the step up in trip while Hillsin's class could tell despite his inconsistency.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Class Performance Revival
scenarios.trigger: If Miss Goldfire recaptures her 2023 spring form on this good ground
scenarios.body: Her prominent racing style positions her perfectly to strike at the business end while her proven ability at this trip and ground combination gives her the tactical edge. The 44-day break could have freshened her up enough to rediscover that winning thread.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Bradman Course Specialist
scenarios.trigger: If Bradman adapts his running style to sit more prominently than usual
scenarios.body: His two course wins here during winter give him intimate knowledge of Fontwell's unique demands, allowing him to position closer to the pace than his recent efforts suggest. The familiarity factor combined with Luke Scott's tactical nous could spring a surprise.

Washington Singer and Jamaicaine must handle the early pace-setting role despite being more natural prominent runners than leaders

Bradman's two course wins came on softer ground conditions compared to today's good going

races.paceDynamic: Flash Man and Tetsworth will contest the early pace, with Flash Man likely more committed given his confirmed front-running style and confidence from his Plumpton win. Tetsworth unseated last time but showed early speed before that exit and should press Flash Man through the early stages. With only two genuine pace-setters in a 14-runner field, they'll create a solid but not excessive gallop over this 2m1½f trip. This moderate pace scenario clearly favours prominent racers and hold-up horses who can capitalize on the expected kick from halfway, making life difficult for the early leaders.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-up horses benefit
scenarios.trigger: If Flash Man and Tetsworth duel early and fade from two out
scenarios.body: The moderate early pace allows closers to get into ideal stalking positions before unleashing late runs. La Cadalora and Cockney Cleopatra can time their challenges perfectly from off the pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front runner dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Flash Man breaks clear early and dictates throughout
scenarios.body: His class advantage over this field allows him to control the race and kick clear when challenged. The lack of genuine early pace pressure lets him settle into an ideal rhythm.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent tracker strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is steady and prominent racers get first run
scenarios.body: Horses like Bahati Bahati and Moscow Star can track the leaders without pressure then pounce. They avoid both the early speed duel and the traffic problems further back.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos helps outsider
scenarios.trigger: If multiple horses make jumping errors or interfere with each other
scenarios.body: The novice nature of this field creates opportunities for unfancied runners to slip through. An improved performance from a bigger-priced horse benefits from the disruption.

races.paceDynamic: Anytrixwilldo and Boys Of Wexford are the confirmed front runners who will dispute the early lead, with both proven pace-forcers over this trip. Their contest should create an honest gallop throughout, particularly with Boys Of Wexford coming off a winning effort where he made all at Taunton. The strong pace will stretch the field over this demanding 3m2f trip at Fontwell, testing stamina reserves in the final half-mile. This race shape clearly favours hold-up horses and prominent racers with proven staying power who can pick up the pieces when the pace-setters weaken.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Finish
scenarios.trigger: If both Anytrixwilldo and Boys Of Wexford go too hard early and tie each other up.
scenarios.body: The strong gallop will find them both out in the closing stages, allowing the patient hold-up horses to sweep past with superior finishing kicks. Gata Ban showed good late work behind Boys Of Wexford last time and gets a longer trip here to suit.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominance
scenarios.trigger: If Boys Of Wexford repeats his Taunton tactics and gets away with controlled fractions.
scenarios.body: His recent win in the visor gives him confidence to dictate terms again, and if he avoids a fierce early duel with Anytrixwilldo he can control the pace. The 6lb rise may not stop him if the pace scenario falls his way.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong enough to tire the leaders but not collapse them completely.
scenarios.body: The horses tracking the early pace will inherit the race as both leaders and hold-up horses struggle with the timing. Land Girl's Luck and Valirann Gold are best positioned to benefit from this moderate pace scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Stamina Test Grind
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is unusually steady early with the leaders taking their time.
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace would make it a sprint finish where class and speed matter more than stamina. This seems unlikely given both front runners' aggressive styles but would favour the higher-rated horses.

races.paceDynamic: No Mean Feat is the only confirmed pace-setter and will get an easy time of it up front with no pressure from rivals who all prefer to come from behind. This creates a slow, steadily-run race where the pace-setter can dictate terms and kick clear when ready. With eight hold-up horses chasing one uncontested leader over 2m3f, front runners and prominent racers have a massive tactical advantage. The lack of early pace strongly favours horses that can race handy or grab an early position.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Front Runner Wins
scenarios.trigger: If No Mean Feat gets the soft lead he's guaranteed to receive
scenarios.body: He can dictate a steady gallop and have plenty left for a decisive move, while the pack behind struggles to make up ground from too far back. His prominent style becomes the winning move in a race devoid of early pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Rally
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes genuinely slow and collapses completely
scenarios.body: The field bunches up turning for home allowing a staying hold-up horse to produce a sustained finish. Answer That or Man Oh Man could benefit from their higher class ratings in a sprint finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Early
scenarios.trigger: If No Mean Feat fails to go forward or gets headed early
scenarios.body: Multiple horses converge on the lead creating a messy, stop-start pace that suits nothing. The race becomes a lottery where any horse getting a clear run could prevail.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Strong Gallop Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If jockeys panic about the lack of pace and force it from the start
scenarios.body: Several hold-up horses get committed earlier than ideal, creating genuine pace that sets up a true staying test. The strongest stayers benefit from the honest gallop.

watchPoints.text: No Mean Feat must be watched for early positioning - if he doesn't go forward immediately the entire race shape changes

Monitor Jacquetta and Anthracite for signs of their usual late fade pattern emerging in the final furlong
Keep eye on how aggressively jockeys ride early - any forcing of pace undermines the front runner's advantage
Watch Rapid Mission's visor debut for any positive response after his poor sequence over hurdles

runners_data.spotlight: Record of 2-7 over fences and he ran a big race in defeat at Exeter (2m3f, good to soft) last month; is also well suited by this track and he should be in the mix again after a short break.

runners_data.name: Mersey Street
runners_data.note: Sole leader with sustainable pace, but Jonjo O'Neill's woeful 0-18 recent record and 45-day break are red flags.
runners_data.comment: In good form at Sedgefield in February but his form slumped at Carlisle last time
runners_data.spotlight: Won at Sedgefield (2m3f, good to soft) in February and was runner-up on his return visit over 2m5f two weeks later; looks interesting on that form but he needs to bounce back from a heavy defeat at Carlisle in March.

runners_data.name: Majestic Moment
runners_data.note: Recent C&D winner whose hold-up style suits perfectly, though 7lb rise for comfortable victory may not stop him.
runners_data.comment: Made it 3-5 over fences with a comfortable win over C&D latest; big player again up 7lb
runners_data.spotlight: 7yo who made it 3-5 over fences when beating 11 rivals in a C&D handicap (good) 12 days ago; up another 7lb but that was a comfortable success and he's open to more progress in this sphere; key player.

runners_data.name: Footloose Man
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning from long 149-day absence, likely to need the run in this competitive heat.
runners_data.comment: 2-6 over fences and was runner-up in bid for a Fontwell double latest; respected on return
runners_data.spotlight: All of his three victories have been at Fontwell including two chase wins over an extended 2m5f (good to soft); beaten 9l when runner-up here in December but that was behind an improver and he's still lightly raced in this sphere; respected back in trip on his return.

races.paceDynamic: Mersey Street will lead from the start with no serious pace rival, setting a controlled tempo that suits his front-running style. The real battle develops behind as I Shut That d'Or, Le Galli Bier, Alto Alto, and Footloose Man all want prominent positions, creating congestion and forcing some wider than ideal. This pace setup heavily favours the hold-up horses - Begin The Luck, Known Warrior, Wellwillya, and Majestic Moment can avoid the early scrimmaging and have clear runs when the pace lifts. The sustainable early fractions and inevitable traffic problems for prominent runners make this a hold-up horse's race.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-up horses dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Mersey Street sets modest fractions and the prominent group gets bottled up turning for home
scenarios.body: The patient riders can pick their way through as the early pace horses tire, with clear runs available in the final furlong. Begin The Luck and Majestic Moment benefit most from their tactical positioning.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent battle succeeds
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent quartet can secure good positions without interference and the pace stays strong enough
scenarios.body: I Shut That d'Or or Alto Alto can sustain their effort when the leaders tire, having avoided the worst of the early congestion. Their class edges tell in a driving finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Mersey Street wires field
scenarios.trigger: If the leader gets an uncontested lead and the prominent group neutralizes each other with early battles
scenarios.body: Mersey Street stretches clear approaching the last fence with the chasers still sorting themselves out behind. His front-running style proves perfectly suited to the race shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace collapses completely
scenarios.trigger: If Mersey Street goes too slowly and no prominent horse takes it up, creating a sprint finish
scenarios.body: The entire field arrives together at the last fence in a cavalry charge finish where ratings and recent form matter most. Majestic Moment's C&D win gives him the edge in a blanket finish.

watchPoints.text: Watch the prominent quartet I Shut That d'Or, Le Galli Bier, Alto Alto, and Footloose Man approaching the turn - if they're racing four-wide it kills their chances.
Monitor Mersey Street's fractions in the first mile - if he goes too fast early he'll set it up for the hold-up horses even more.
Check how quickly Begin The Luck and Majestic Moment can get into contention turning for home - their positioning will determine the winner.
Watch for interference at the third last fence where the prominent group typically starts making their moves and traffic becomes critical.
Observe jockey Freddie Mitchell's positioning on Le Galli Bier - his inexperience could cost valuable lengths in the crucial phases.
